From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Overall assessment:** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced." It combines a low cap, a short claims window, collapse of fundamental warranties into the general regime, blanket general disclosure of the data room, a sweeping knowledge qualifier, and deferral of two completion-critical items (Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge) to post-Completion — while leaving AUD 420,000 of bonuses out of the funds flow. Several of these interact to make the warranty package close to worthless. Also note the Disclosure Letter is dated by reference to a 22 September 2026 data room cut-off; it must be brought down to signing/Completion.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- *Buyer wants:* 100% of price for general warranties; at minimum 50% given the identified risk profile (Bluefen 30% revenue concentration, unresolved privacy incident, unverified IP chain).
- *Recommendation:* Counter at 100%, fallback 50%; carve Title/Capacity, Tax, IP and specific indemnities out entirely. **Reason:** A 20% cap on a business with several live, unquantified exposures leaves the Buyer under-protected relative to risk already visible in DD.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (deductible).
- *Buyer wants:* De minimis ~AUD 10,000 (0.04%); basket ~AUD 120,000–240,000 (0.5–1%); tipping (first-dollar) basket; related claims aggregated for de minimis.
- *Recommendation:* Reject deductible; propose AUD 10k / AUD 240k tipping basket with aggregation of related claims. **Reason:** A deductible structure means the Buyer silently absorbs the first AUD 250,000 of every warranty breach on top of the cap and knowledge qualifiers.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months from Completion; limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- *Buyer wants:* 24 months general (covering two audit cycles); 7 years tax; 6 years fundamental/title and IP; indemnity claims not time-limited beyond statutory limitation.
- *Recommendation:* 24 months general; separate longer periods for tax/title/IP; delete the "all Claims" default. **Reason:** 18 months may not capture a full post-Completion audit cycle, and the default sweep would quietly apply the short period to indemnities and fundamental warranties.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity and title warranties subject to same cap and time limits as general warranties ("administrative simplicity").
- *Buyer wants:* Title/capacity/authority warranties capped at 100% of price (or uncapped), 6-year (or statutory) limitation, no de minimis/basket, no knowledge qualifier.
- *Recommendation:* Reject outright. **Reason:** If title fails the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing — recovering only AUD 4.8m within 18 months is not "simplicity," it is a transfer of the core deal risk to the Buyer.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* No fraud carve-out stated; cls 9.3/12.8/20.5 say limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- *Buyer wants:* Express carve-out from every limitation (cap, thresholds, time, exclusive remedy, non-reliance, knowledge) for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default by the Seller or its officers.
- *Recommendation:* Insert a mandatory fraud carve-out; non-negotiable. **Reason:** Attempting to limit liability for fraud is unenforceable in practice and its absence signals a drafting posture the Buyer should not accept.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records"; Disclosure Letter §1.4 disclaims any admission.
- *Buyer wants:* Disclosure only of matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter"; data room disclosed only to extent indexed and listed in a schedule; no disclosure of public registers (or limited to ASIC/PPSR/IP Australia/title searches on a specified date).
- *Recommendation:* Replace with a "fair disclosure" standard and a scheduled, indexed data room; reject public-records disclosure. **Reason:** Blanket disclosure of an unindexed data room and all public registers effectively disapplies the warranties, since any breach could be said to be "disclosed" somewhere.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* No claim for any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- *Buyer wants:* Delete; or at most limit to actual knowledge of a named small deal-team list, excluding advisers and excluding constructive/"discoverable" knowledge, and never applying to specific indemnities.
- *Recommendation:* Delete cl 8.3; fallback to actual knowledge of 2–3 named individuals, expressly not covering matters within the specific indemnities. **Reason:** "Discoverable" knowledge imputed through advisers, the data room and public records converts the warranties into a due diligence exercise with no residual Seller risk allocation — and it compounds the SPA-N-006 problem.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- *Seller:* "Reasonable endeavours"; condition satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent; Disclosure Letter confirms no final consent and no evidence of cl 11.3 conditions being satisfied. Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue.
- *Buyer wants:* Condition precedent in Buyer's favour: unconditional written consent under cl 11.2, on terms reasonably acceptable to Buyer, with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied (or waived in writing by Bluefen); Seller "best endeavours"; Buyer-only waiver right; termination right if not satisfied by long-stop.
- *Recommendation:* Harden to a Buyer-waivable CP with Buyer-approval of consent form; consider price adjustment/escrow if Bluefen revenue is lost within 12 months. **Reason:** Losing 30% of revenue at Completion is an existential value issue, and a consent "delivered" but conditional is no consent at all.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion"; Disclosure Letter confirms no repayment and no security discharge.
- *Buyer wants:* Repayment and discharge at Completion as a completion deliverable: payout letter from Riverlark, executed deed of release, PPSR discharge, with payout amount deducted from the purchase price under the debt-free/cash-free mechanism and paid directly to Riverlark from Buyer's funds.
- *Recommendation:* Reject post-Completion release; make payout/discharge a Completion deliverable in the funds flow. **Reason:** "Debt-free/cash-free" is meaningless if the Buyer acquires a company still owing AUD 3.2m to a secured lender with a change-of-control trigger (cl 8.1) that may be breached by Completion itself.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in funds flow; on-costs not disclosed.
- *Buyer wants:* Bonuses plus superannuation, payroll tax and employer on-costs treated as Transaction Expenses/Debt-like items, deducted from price in the funds flow, or paid by the Company pre-Completion from Seller-funded cash with a specific indemnity.
- *Recommendation:* Require itemisation in funds flow as a price deduction including grossed-up on-costs (budget ~AUD 480–500k); add specific indemnity for any shortfall. **Reason:** Because the bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, they crystallise as a Company liability post-Completion — i.e. the Buyer pays them unless the price is adjusted.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the AUD 180,000 SOW3 payment; "considered adequate."
- *Buyer wants:* Pre-Completion payment of SOW3 fees with receipt, plus executed confirmatory assignment of SOW3 Project Materials from Ironquay (cl 7.3 condition); failing that, a specific uncapped (or 100%-capped) indemnity covering loss of title to the IP, re-development costs, third-party claims and lost revenue, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge qualifier and with a 6-year period.
- *Recommendation:* Make payment + confirmatory assignment a Completion deliverable; retain indemnity for title/usage loss, not just the AUD 180k. **Reason:** The exposure is not the unpaid fee but non-ownership of the Project Materials — the indemnity as drafted covers the wrong risk.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material"; Disclosure Letter confirms ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address, scope and access unknown, notification question unresolved.
- *Buyer wants:* Completed investigation before signing (or at least before Completion); legal advice on Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme obligations; evidence of recipient deletion/undertaking; specific indemnity for all costs, regulator fines/penalties, notification costs, customer claims and remediation, uncapped or capped at a meaningful amount, outside the basket, 6-year period, not subject to knowledge or disclosure.
- *Recommendation:* Specific indemnity plus pre-Completion investigation and sign-off; consider escrow/retention (e.g. AUD 500k–1m) pending OAIC position. **Reason:** The Seller's own disclosure admits it cannot establish access, scope or notifiability — "not material" is an assertion, not a finding, and the Buyer inherits the regulatory exposure.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- *Seller:* Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs"; Disclosure Letter declines to say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.
- *Buyer wants:* Confirmation of commitment dates and termination rights; if renewals were triggered/accelerated pre-Completion or are prepayments, treat as Debt-like/Transaction Expense or working capital adjustment; conduct-of-business covenant requiring Buyer consent to enter/renew commitments > AUD 50k between signing and Completion.
- *Recommendation:* Obtain DD-008/DD-011 contract analysis; adjust price if accrued/unavoidable; otherwise cover via working capital peg and interim covenants. **Reason:** Three identical related renewals split under a single threshold is a classic pattern for avoiding disclosure/consent thresholds, and the Seller's refusal to characterise them is itself a red flag.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- *Seller:* One regime: all limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cls 9.3, 12.3, 12.8, 20.5), including fundamental, tax, IP and indemnity claims.
- *Buyer wants:* Separate regimes: (a) General Warranties — cap/basket/de minimis/24 months; (b) Fundamental Warranties — 100%, 6 years, no thresholds; (c) Tax Warranties & Tax Indemnity — 100%, 7 years, no thresholds; (d) Specific Indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Bluefen) — outside all limitations and knowledge/disclosure qualifiers; (e) fraud — unlimited.
- *Recommendation:* Restructure Schedule/cl 12 into separate limitation categories; delete the "all Claims" sweep. **Reason:** The single regime is the structural mechanism that neuters every other protection the Buyer negotiates — fix this first.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced solely by the Company share register (DD-012); Disclosure Letter notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent verification: ASIC current and historical company extract, share certificate(s), PPSR search against Company and Seller (noting Riverlark security), review of constitution/shareholders' agreements for pre-emptive rights or transfer restrictions, confirmation of no options/convertibles, Seller board/shareholder approvals, and a full title warranty unaffected by this disclosure.
- *Recommendation:* Run the searches now (pre-signing) and make Seller warrant title unconditionally with no disclosure against it. **Reason:** A self-maintained register is not proof of title, and the Seller is clearly positioning this disclosure to argue later that the Buyer "knew" the register was the only evidence.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* "Settled under the general regime" — i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, basket, knowledge/disclosure qualifiers.
- *Buyer wants:* Full tax warranties plus a stand-alone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, 7-year period, 100% cap, no basket); IP warranties on ownership, validity, no infringement, open-source compliance, employee/contractor assignments — 6 years, 100% cap, with the Ironquay matter specifically indemnified.
- *Recommendation:* Treat as not settled; table full tax indemnity and IP warranty schedule in the mark-up. **Reason:** For an analytics business the IP is the asset and tax liabilities surface over ATO amendment periods (4+ years) — neither can sit inside an 18-month, 20% regime.

---

## Priority order for the mark-up
1. **Structural:** SPA-N-014 (category separation), SPA-N-005 (fraud), SPA-N-006/007 (disclosure & knowledge) — without these, the rest doesn't bite.
2. **Completion mechanics / price:** SPA-N-009 (Riverlark at Completion), SPA-N-010 (bonuses in funds flow), SPA-N-008 (Bluefen CP), SPA-N-011 (Ironquay assignment).
3. **Risk-specific:** SPA-N-012 (privacy indemnity/retention), SPA-N-013 (Sandbar), SPA-N-015 (title searches now).
4. **Economic terms:** SPA-N-001/002/003/004/016.

**Additional action items:** (i) require a bring-down of the Disclosure Letter to signing and Completion (current data room cut-off is 22 Sept 2026 — six weeks stale); (ii) request Seller's position on W&I insurance if they hold firm on 20% — the Buyer should not fund the premium for a policy needed because of Seller-side limitations; (iii) consider a retention/escrow of ~AUD 1.5–2.4m (6–10%) for 18–24 months given the number of unquantified exposures.

- *Seller:* One regime: all limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cls 9.3, 12.3, 12.8, 20.5), including fundamental, tax, IP and indemnity claims.
- *Buyer wants:* Separate regimes: (a) General Warranties — cap/basket/de minimis/24 months; (b) Fundamental Warranties — 100%, 6 years, no thresholds; (c) Tax Warranties & Tax Indemnity — 100%, 7 years, no thresholds; (d) Specific Indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Bluefen) — outside all limitations and knowledge/disclosure qualifiers; (e) fraud — unlimited.
- *Recommendation:* Restructure Schedule/cl 12 into separate limitation categories; delete the "all Claims" sweep. **Reason:** The single regime is the structural mechanism that neuters every other protection the Buyer negotiates — fix this first.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced solely by the Company share register (DD-012); Disclosure Letter notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent verification: ASIC current and historical company extract, share certificate(s), PPSR search against Company and Seller (noting Riverlark security), review of constitution/shareholders' agreements for pre-emptive rights or transfer restrictions, confirmation of no options/convertibles, Seller board/shareholder approvals, and a full title warranty unaffected by this disclosure.
- *Recommendation:* Run the searches now (pre-signing) and make Seller warrant title unconditionally with no disclosure against it. **Reason:** A self-maintained register is not proof of title, and the Seller is clearly positioning this disclosure to argue later that the Buyer "knew" the register was the only evidence.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* "Settled under the general regime" — i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, basket, knowledge/disclosure qualifiers.
- *Buyer wants:* Full tax warranties plus a stand-alone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, 7-year period, 100% cap, no basket); IP warranties on ownership, validity, no infringement, open-source compliance, employee/contractor assignments — 6 years, 100% cap, with the Ironquay matter specifically indemnified.
- *Recommendation:* Treat as not settled; table full tax indemnity and IP warranty schedule in the mark-up. **Reason:** For an analytics business the IP is the asset and tax liabilities surface over ATO amendment periods (4+ years) — neither can sit inside an 18-month, 20% regime.
